title: Why Nvidia's 37% Crash Hits Your 401(k)
description:
Is the AI bubble bursting, and what does it mean for your 401(k)? If you own an S&P 500 index fund, about $6.05 of every $100 is Nvidia, and Nvidia's stock fell 37.6% from its Oct 6 high ($239.24) to $149.30 on Nov 25, 2026, after a +31.5% one-day jump on Nov 23. Explained simply: what's inside $100 of an index fund (the top 10 holdings, 9 companies, are $36.96), your hidden AI slice (~$25), what the drop cost every $100, the comeback math, and what 24 S&P 500 drops of 10%+ since 1950 say about getting back (median about 14 months, price only).

- State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) daily holdings, as of Nov 24, 2026: https://www.ssga.com/us/en/intermediary/library-content/products/fund-data/etfs/us/holdings-daily-us-en-spy.xlsx
- Associated Press market report, Nov 25, 2026 (intraday S&P 500 -3.2%, Nasdaq -4.6% at the lows; news report, not official data).
- History of 10%+ declines: our own count from S&P 500 daily closes since 1950 (Yahoo Finance ^GSPC), price only, before dividends.
Weights are as of Nov 24 and move every day; the 'cost per $100' math is approximate. Jordan and Priya are a made-up example household; the $500-a-month contribution is a worked example.

This video is education only, not financial advice. Past performance does not predict future results.
Original script and animation; no real people or logos. Narrated with an AI voice.
